transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's very nice to meet you too, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. 

Well, I suppose what brings me in is... I've just always been the kind of guy who's constantly moving from one thing to the next. I just have a hard time sitting completely idle. Which usually isn't a bad thing, right? It just means I like to keep busy! But, um, my job—I do customer service—we recently got a new work setup, and it's... well, it's made this little habit of mine a lot harder to hide, I guess. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and not bothering anyone. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing I should be bringing up?
Since you were a child, have you often had trouble staying focused on tasks?

Well, as a kid, I suppose I had my moments, just like any boy, you know? I was always eager to get out and play. But, um, looking at things now... I wouldn't say it's a huge problem or anything. 

It's just... well, for example, in our longer coaching meetings at work, or when I'm supposed to be reading a new procedure, I always start off just fine. I really do try to give it my full attention, I promise. But after a few minutes, I'll sort of realize that my eyes kept moving down the page or I've been looking right at the manager, but I didn't actually take in a word of what was just said. 

I'm sure that's pretty normal when things get a little dry, right? I mean, everyone's mind wanders a bit. I hope that's the kind of example you were looking for, Doctor. Am I answering your questions okay?
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or wired for several days in a row?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I mean, I have days where I feel pretty good and get a lot done, but I wouldn't say I ever feel "wired" or anything extreme. Just normal good days, you know? I definitely don't have periods where I'm bouncing off the walls for days on end or anything that would be, um, concerning. I hope that's a good thing to hear, Doctor? Is that a normal response?
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try to ignore them?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, my mind is always sort of hopping from one thing to the next, like I mentioned, but it's never really anything upsetting or unwanted. Just regular everyday stuff, you know? Like whether I need to pick up milk on the way home or if I finished a customer's ticket right. 

I definitely don't have anything bad or strange getting stuck in my head that I can't shake off. Is that what you meant by that question, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm understanding you correctly and giving you the right information.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, sure, working in customer service, you have your stressful moments—like if a caller is really upset or the phones are backing up—but I don't just sit around worrying for no reason. I try to just take things as they come, you know? Keep a positive attitude. 

I definitely don't have that kind of anxiety where I'm fretting over nothing at all. I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying my best to give you a clear picture, Doctor. Am I being helpful with these answers?
Before you turned 12, did you often have the same kind of trouble paying attention or sitting still?

Well, um... I guess if I really think back, yeah, it's been around for a long time. Definitely way before I started this current position. I don't want it to sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I wasn't getting into major trouble. But, you know, I remember my grade school teachers writing on my report cards that I was bright, which is nice... but they'd also say I was a bit careless with my work. And, um, I guess I did talk out of turn sometimes and they had to remind me to just stay focused on what I was doing. 

It wasn't terrible, just... typical boy stuff, maybe? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a problem student. Does that kind of thing help you understand my situation better, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern since childhood of inattentive and hyperactive/restless behavior, including difficulty sustaining attention during meetings/reading, careless work, talking out of turn, and difficulty sitting still/constantly moving. Onset before age 12 is supported by grade school report card comments. Bipolar-spectrum, OCD, and generalized anxiety features were screened and denied. Although impairment is described mainly in the work setting and the interview does not fully establish all subtype-specific criteria, the presentation is most consistent with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, unspecified.
